title: DORA Community Discussion - State of AI-assisted Software Development
summary: DORA team presents its 2025 State of AI-assisted Software Development report: near-universal adoption, AI as an amplifier, throughput up but instability up, and seven capabilities that amplify AI's benefits.

assertions.quote: Google says 90% of of AI uh 90% of of software developers are using AI at work.

verdicts.note: Stack Overflow 2025: ~84% use or plan to use AI tools, about half of professionals daily; JetBrains and DORA report similar figures.

assertions.quote: AI's primary role in software development is that of an amplifier.

verdicts.note: DORA 2025 data shows AI outcomes depend on surrounding capabilities, which supports the framing, though 'amplifier' is an interpretation of correlational survey results.

assertions.quote: we continue to see an increase in software delivery instability ility in relationship to AI adoption

verdicts.note: DORA 2025 reports AI adoption now positively associated with throughput while still associated with higher delivery instability (change failure and rework).

assertions.quote: we're seeing the majority of folks are saying that AI actually improved code quality.

verdicts.note: DORA 2025 found ~59% reporting positive quality impact; it's self-report, which other studies show overstates measured effects.

assertions.quote: a clear and communicated AI stance, a healthy data ecosystem, AI accessible internal data, strong version control practices, working in small batches

verdicts.note: These come from DORA's 2025 AI capabilities model, a survey-based correlational analysis; plausible and consistent with older DORA findings on small batches, but not causal evidence.

assertions.quote: highquality platforms are essential to unlocking the organizational value of AI and also essential to managing the associated risks.

verdicts.note: DORA 2025 reports this association, but it is correlational survey evidence and platform quality is hard to separate from overall engineering maturity.

assertions.quote: instead of using AI to say generate more code that just piles up and piles up due to a bottleneck like code review

verdicts.note: Studies of developer time show coding is a minority of work; DORA and Faros 2025 found individual coding gains often don't translate into delivery throughput.

assertions.quote: AI adoption on its own has a modest impact on organizations performance

verdicts.note: DORA 2024/25 and Faros 2025 found individual output up while organizational delivery metrics stayed flat or worsened; review and integration become the bottleneck.
